title: Warm-handshake sleuthing diary: dedicated GPU pool warmup anomaly
content:
Location: dedicated-gpu-pool (pool-id: dp-7a3)
Summary: Intermittent failures during node warm-handshake/priming. Symptoms: repeated warm failures for new CUDNN-backed instances causing autoscaler to oscillate and leaving capacity underutilized while latency SLOs degrade. This is a personal working log — scratchpad, commands, outputs, early hypotheses.

Timeline (high level)
- 2025-11-02 09:12 UTC: Pager alert - p95 token latency spike (hosted tenants using dp-7a3)
- 2025-11-02 09:15 UTC: Autoscaler fired scale-up +4; 2/4 nodes entered Ready but long RPC priming time (~90s)
- 2025-11-02 09:18 UTC: Several 'handshake' errors in node-init logs: 'kv-cache priming timeout' and 'inference-runtime handshake failed: timed out'
- 2025-11-02 ongoing: Observed churn for next ~45m; some nodes eventually become warm, others never finish handshake and get recycled.

First-pass commands and raw snippets (notes to self)
- k get nodes -l pool=dp-7a3 -o wide
  -> two nodes in NotReady for ~120s (reason: kubelet, but service logs show runtime reply delay)

- kubectl logs -n redwood runtime-init-xyz --tail=200
  -> ... INFO: priming kv-cache: prefix=\"/models/gpt2\"
  -> ERROR: handshake failure: rpc call failed: context deadline exceeded

- curl -sS -X POST https://control-plane/redwood/pools/dp-7a3/diagnostics -d '{"probe":"handshake"}'
  -> {status: "queued", job: "diag-241"}

- diag results (excerpt):
  * socket/connect: OK
  * model-shard-download: OK
  * kv-cache-init: 1/3 shards timed out
  * tls_handshake: OK
  * runtime-health: degraded (memory pressure transient)

Grepped stack traces (timestamps aligned):
- runtime-worker[23]: WARN: shard 2 failed to map to GPU memory: out-of-memory? trying mmap fallback
- runtime[main]: ERR: post-warm RPC to control-plane returned 503 (service busy)

Quick checks I ran locally
- confirmed kernel driver versions on failed nodes: nvidia-driver 535.86 / cuda 12.1 (matches golden)
- compared /etc/sysctl.conf - no divergence
- dsync of deps: container images passed checksum

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Race between kv-cache priming and model kv-shard binding. If priming stalls on a shard, handshake waits and times out. (evidence: kv-cache-init shows 1/3 shards timed out)
2) Transient memory spike during priming causing OOM fallback -> slower priming -> handshake timeout. (evidence: "failed to map to GPU memory" logs)
3) Control-plane backpressure: runtime waiting for model-serving token from central control plane; if control plane overloaded, handshakes back off and autoscaler keeps retrying. (evidence: 503 responses in logs)
4) Scheduler soft-affinity bug: new nodes are assigned hot workloads before kv-cache is primed causing immediate memory pressure + thrash. (less direct evidence)

Mitigations tried (and outcomes)
- bump handshake timeout from 30s -> 90s (canary): reduced immediate recycle but latency tail persisted (nodes stay in warm-pending longer, but eventually finish)
- force prefetch of all kv-shards at image bootstrap stage (local build): reduced shard timeouts in single-node test but caused memory pressure reproducibly under synthetic load
- control-plane rate-limit smoothing: temporarily lowered client concurrency for priming RPCs; observed fewer 503s and fewer handshake failures in next 2 hours

Repro steps (local cluster)
1) Spin up M1-sized node with same instance-type and attach to test pool dp-test-01
2) Deploy runtime image with debug flags (RT_DEBUG=kv,RT_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT=30)
3) Run script to emulate 10 concurrent priming requests: `scripts/prime-batch.sh --count 10 --model gpt2-small`
4) Observe logs: grep for 'kv-cache-init' and 'handshake'

Minimal reproduction script (rough)
- `prime-batch.sh`
  for i in `seq 1 $1`; do 
    curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/prime -d '{"model":"gpt2-small"}' &
  done
  wait

Observed in repro: when count >=6, shard 2 consistently times out in ~40% runs. Reproduces handshake timeout.

Ideas + experiments to try next
- Instrument shard-level timings (break down priming into download, mmap, copy-to-gpu). Add histogram metrics for each step.
- Try eager mmap fallback earlier: attempt mmap earlier to avoid large temporary allocations on CUDA pinning step. Danger: may increase fragmentation.
- Add exponential backoff on autoscaler for pools that have >X% warm-pending nodes to avoid oscillation (short term mitigation).
- Push a control-plane smoothing window to avoid 503 bursts during cluster boots.
- Create a canary pool with RT_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT=120 and kv-prefetch disabled, to test tradeoff between latency tail vs. capacity availability.

Notes for postmortem (if this escalates)
- capture full diag outputs for nodes (diag-241 id) and correlate with control-plane request logs (timestamps in UTC)
- compute correlation between number of concurrent priming jobs and percent of shard timeouts (metric: priming_concurrency vs kv_shard_timeouts)
- annotate autoscaler policy that allowed immediate scale-up without minimum priming window

Sticky observations / weirdness
- Some nodes show 'failed to map to GPU memory' only for specific shard indices (2 & 5) — could be allocation pattern interplay with mmap alignment.
- When I manually restarted runtime on failed node, it sometimes succeeded immediately, implying transient external factor.
- Manual increase of RT_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT masks the issue but doesn't fix root cause.

Open TODOs (priority order)
- [ ] Add per-shard timing telemetry (traces) - Lina to pick up (ticket RDW-5490)
- [ ] Autoscaler policy tweak: min-warm-window=60s - Marco to prototype in test cluster
- [ ] Control-plane ingress smoothing: ops to test rollback of recent rate-limit config change (linked in PR)
- [ ] Run memory-profiling on priming path with synthetic heavy concurrent priming workload

Random scratch / commands I might want to keep
- watch -n1 'kubectl get pods -l pool=dp-7a3 -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PHASE:.status.phase,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp'
- journalctl -u runtime.service -f | grep -i 'kv-cache\|handshake\|mmap'
- python3 -c 'import requests; r=requests.post("https://control-plane/redwood/pools/dp-7a3/diagnostics",json={"probe":"handshake"}); print(r.text)'

Notes to self: prioritize quick mitigations (autoscaler backoff + control-plane smoothing) to stop customer impact, then instrument and iterate. Keep this doc as a running breadcrumb log; will tidy for a postmortem if we confirm root cause.

End of scratchpad entry (2025-12-18).
